summary: Full e2e testing of the Daily Rashifal feature. 6/6 pytest backend tests pass. Playwright UI test confirms the rashifal tile renders inside #panchang-section with all 12 pills in the correct Aries→Pisces order, default pill matches today's Moon sign (Libra), and clicking a different pill updates the forecast text. Regression on /api/panchang/today and /api/festivals/upcoming is clean.
critical_code_review_comments: rashifal.py _fallback_forecasts uses RASHIS.index((name,sanskrit,lord,glyph)) inside the zip loop to look up lucky_color/number — O(n^2). Works (12 items) but the idiomatic fix is to use enumerate() over RASHIS, or pre-zip the lucky_color/number lists. Cosmetic, not a bug.

The cache in rashifal.py is unbounded module-level dict keyed by (date, tz). In practice it self-prunes because stale keys are simply never read again, but over long uptime across many timezones it will grow. Low priority.
If EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is missing, _generate_via_claude returns None silently and the tile shows source='fallback'. Consider logging a warning so ops can notice missing config.
All interactive elements in RashifalTile already have data-testid — good testability coverage.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_rashifal.py covers rashifal endpoint (default tz, cache hit <2s, invalid tz→400, alt tz America/New_York) plus regression on panchang/festivals. First rashifal call took ~41s (AI path → source='ai', moon in Libra on 2026-05-01). Cached subsequent calls returned instantly. The AI batched JSON parsed cleanly — source='ai' confirmed both via API and UI meta ('AI-AUTHORED'). Pills are all 12 and in correct order. Default selected pill = today's moon sign (Libra). Clicking aries vs pisces produced distinct forecasts.
